newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Ex-justice minister to Israel's Netanyahu cleared.
newsitem.headline: Ex-justice minister to Israel's Netanyahu cleared.

text.p: An Israeli court acquitted former justice minister Yaacov Neeman on Thursday, raising speculation he might return to the job in place of his embattled successor.

Neeman was cleared of charges he obstructed justice and lied under oath. His indictment last August forced him to leave the job he had been given by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu less than two months earlier.
At the time Netanyahu said he hoped Neeman would return quickly to his post. He appointed Likud legislator Tzachi Hanegbi "to temporarily fill the position".
Asked on Thursday if Netanyahu would take Neeman back as justice minister, the prime minister's spokesman Shai Bazak said: "It's too early to say".
Asked about his plans after the acquittal, Neeman told reporters at the courthouse that he would "wait and see".

Opposition legislators and members of Netanyahu's own government have called for Hanegbi's dismissal since police recommended last month he be tried for corruption in the ill-fated appointment of an attorney-general in January.
Police had also recommended Netanyahu be charged but state prosecuters decided not to indict the two, citing insufficient evidence.
